correctness.rationale: The first enumerated value in each nonempty row defines partial computable g, and the existence of two different outputs is c.e., providing the exact erasure B. Conversely, enumerate (x,g(x)), then a distinct value after an erasure witness; yields singleton precisely outside B. Every c.e. difference A∖C is realized by a constant-zero partial selector on A and erasures A∩C. For composition, l=k∘g is partial computable and E=(B∩dom(l))∪{x∈dom(l):g(x)∈D} is c.e.; l restricted outside E equals the extensional composite. A total selector must be total computable; noncomputable c.e. K gives d.c.e. domain examples and d.c.e. graph of noncomputable total characteristic function. Independent 512 finite relation and 262144 composition checks corroborate set identities, not Turing-effectiveness proof.
